c.tagline: Atlantic surf meets resilient history on Liberia's coast.

taxi.fareNote: Shared taxis run fixed routes for a flat per-seat fare (agree on the amount before boarding); private/chartered taxis are negotiated since none are metered.

emergency.police: 911 (unreliable; response times vary greatly and calls may go unanswered)
emergency.medical: 911, or go directly to the nearest hospital (e.g. JFK Medical Center, Redemption Hospital) — ambulances are poorly equipped and slow
emergency.note: Emergency response in Monrovia is slow and inconsistent; for medical emergencies a taxi or private car to the hospital is often faster than waiting for an ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: Monrovia's diplomatic and NGO hub on a breezy oceanfront headland, packed with embassies and the city's longest-running upscale hotels; best for business travelers and aid workers wanting security and sea views.

The historic commercial core along Broad and Ashmun Streets, with markets, government buildings, and budget-to-midrange hotels; suited to travelers on a tight budget who want to be within walking distance of the action.
A leafy corridor along Tubman Boulevard and UN Drive lined with embassies, UN offices and NGOs; a quieter, more residential base popular with longer-term aid and development workers.
A growing residential-commercial strip east of Sinkor toward the ELWA junction, with newer serviced apartments and mid-range hotels; good for self-catering travelers and longer stays.

The coastal highway corridor toward Roberts International Airport, dotted with beach resorts and airport-convenient properties; ideal for travelers with early flights or wanting a beach escape outside the city center.

water.note: Tap water is not recommended for visitors; use bottled or treated water.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor; shared taxis and minibuses charge a flat fare per route or per seat, with no card or ticketing system in use.
transit.hours: Informal service roughly 6am-9pm; little to no public transport after dark, when travel by private or hired vehicle is strongly advised.
transit.note: Monrovia has no metro, tram, or formal bus network — transport relies on shared yellow taxis and privately run 'money bus' minibuses on fixed routes, plus 'pehn-pehn' motorcycle taxis for short hops.

bus: Cess Trans (regional coaches to Sierra Leone, Guinea and Côte d'Ivoire)
Local 'money bus' minibuses on fixed city routes
ferry: Informal water taxis across the Mesurado and St. Paul Rivers to Bushrod Island/New Kru Town

airport.name: Roberts International Airport (ROB)
airport.drive: 60-90 min via the Robertsfield Highway (longer in heavy rain or traffic)

transit.m: Shared taxi into Monrovia (~1.5-2 hrs, shared with other passengers)
Private/chartered taxi direct to city center

tip.r: Tipping isn't deeply rooted in local custom but is increasingly expected at upscale hotels and restaurants; round up taxi fares and leave roughly 5-10% at nicer sit-down restaurants unless a service charge is already included.
